comments.title: Paging runs on the server, not in the browser
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.70 — Paging runs on the server, not in the browser

**Not taken:** keep the bare list; page and sort client-side with MatTableDataSource

**Why:** The owners grid (#25) paged on the server, and visits grow without bound. The ticket says only "paginated", and the browser-side version needed no API break, which pulls this down.

comments.title: Default view is the 10 latest visits
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.90 — Default view is the 10 latest visits

**Not taken:** the first page in id or ascending-date order

**Why:** The grid already sorted newest first before paging, so this keeps what users saw. Ten is the middle of the three sizes the ticket names.

comments.title: API caps the page size at 100, not at the three UI sizes
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.65 — API caps the page size at 100, not at the three UI sizes

**Not taken:** reject any size other than 5, 10 or 20 in the API too

**Why:** It copies the owners endpoint (MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100), and the ticket describes the grid, not the API. A stricter reading of "5, 10, or 20" would hold the API to it too.

comments.title: Owner column sorts by first name, then last name
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.75 — Owner column sorts by first name, then last name

**Not taken:** sort by last name, as a clinic register usually does

**Why:** The cell reads "First Last", so this sort matches what is shown, and owners' Name sort does the same. A clinic looking people up by surname would want last name first.

comments.title: Ties within a sorted column fall back to latest first, then id
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.60 — Ties within a sorted column fall back to latest first, then id

**Not taken:** tie-break by id only, as the owners grid does

**Why:** When one pet has several visits, showing them chronologically is the useful order, and the id still makes paging stable. Nobody asked for it, so a plain id tie-break is equally defensible.

comments.title: No index added for the date sort
comments.anchor: @Query(value = "SELECT v FROM Visit v JOIN FETCH v.pet p JOIN FETCH p.owner",
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.50 — No index added for the date sort

**Not taken:** a Flyway migration indexing visits(visit_date, id)

**Why:** The seed has 28 visits and the ticket does not mention scale. If volume grows, sorting the whole table per page will show up, so this is a coin flip on when.
